citation: 'Prairie Avenue and Twentieth Street.' Wood engraving (Blomgren Bros. & Co.), A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, vol. 3 (Chicago, 1886), p. 65.
author: A. T. Andreas (publisher); Blomgren Bros. & Co. (engravers)

note: The style library's Italianate plate. It shows a two-storey block with elaborate window crowns, a bracketed cornice and a tall square entrance tower with a belvedere, behind an iron fence: the Allerton house, which stood until about 1915 and so in 1904 (the Prairie library), but is not yet built in the 1904 scene. No source read names its style; the 1973 Landmarks report describes 'two high stories of expensive detail topped by a tower that rose another full story', so the style is graded Inferred on the PHMC guide's features. Andreas's engravings are published views and are graded as tier 5 illustrations in this project, as its other Andreas plates are.
what_it_supplies: a public-domain view of an Italianate house on Prairie Avenue, with its tower, window crowns and bracketed cornice
